title: Where San Francisco fits in Lyft’s $272.5 million driver settlement

beats.text: Lyft signed a proposed $272.5 million driver settlement.

visual.sub: A $272.5 million agreement addressed work performed before the classification law changed

beats.text: The case covers driving before Proposition 22 changed the rules.

visual.kicker: A $272.5 million agreement addressed work performed before the classification law changed

beats.text: Lyft gave nearly $49 million to the committee supporting the change.

visual.kicker: Lyft backed the ballot measure. Statewide and San Francisco voters split.

beats.text: California voted yes. San Francisco voted no.
Four government offices would split the civil penalties equally.

visual.kicker: San Francisco’s proposed penalty share works out to $5,109,375

beats.text: San Francisco’s proposed share comes to just over $5 million.
More than 1,600 drivers who filed individual wage claims would receive extra compensation.

visual.kicker: Claimants and other drivers would receive different payments

beats.text: Their eligible miles would count twice when the rest was divided.
More than 1,900 drivers objected, according to their organization.

visual.kicker: The judge asked what workers could realistically recover and when payments would arrive

beats.text: The judge asked what drivers could realistically recover at trial.

visual.kicker: The judge asked what workers could realistically recover and when payments would arrive

beats.text: The November 6 filing announced another hearing. A signed judgment would trigger the first payment.
